text:
perf-bot: ALERT: nightly-ci small-batch benchmark p95 increased by 28% vs baseline for 13c2d1 -> 0xabc123. Artifact: s3://redwood-nightly/2765437890/bench.tar.gz :warning:

marta: seeing this now, thanks. I kicked off a quick repro locally but wanted to check if anyone already started a bisect. 

ken: not yet — I'm on call but can pick this up in ~20m. any obvious suspects? cache invalidation or scheduler changes? :thinking_face:

devon: I ran the flamegraph from the perf bot payload — looks like KV cache miss spikes around step 4. attaching snippet of the flame output below.

devon: ```
# top stacks (collapsed)
runtime::dispatch;kv_cache::lookup_miss  42%
runtime::attention;matmul::kernel        18%
rpc::serialize                           12%
```

bri: I noticed the cache liveness patch landed yesterday (PR #431). That touched eviction logic. Could be related. 

marta: ok let's triage: plan -> (1) reproduce on nightly harness with --deterministic-kv=on/off (2) run quick bisect against the 6 commits between baseline and 0xabc123 (3) collect pprof + flame for the slow runs and upload to the artifact store. 

ken: I'm starting step 1 now. command I'm running: ```./infra/bench/run.sh --profile small-batch --commit 0xabc123 --runs 3 --save-artifacts /tmp/2765437890```

ken: pinging @opsbot for extra GPU pool in case we need parallel bisect runs. :rocket: 

opsbot: resource-request accepted — 2xT4 pool reserved for 1h, label=nightly-triage-2765437890.

devon: while ken runs, I'll diff the eviction changes. early glance: we added a background cleanup that increments eviction_frequency when hit_rate < 0.6. maybe too aggressive under small-batch patterns.

marta: good call. devon, can you add a quick revert patch to test locally? if that's fast we can validate hypothesis before full bisect.

devon: will do. pushing a test branch now: `git checkout -b devon/kv-eviction-probe && git revert 7f3d9e2` — should be ready in ~10m.

bri: FYI I ran one harness with deterministic-kv=off and saw p95 hold close to baseline. when I flipped deterministic-kv=on the p95 regressed. suggests cache behavior matters.

marta: helpful. ken — if your run reproduces, let's collect `pprof` heap+cpu at the slow window and upload with tag `triage-2765437890`. example: 
```
pprof --seconds=30 --output=/tmp/pprof-2765437890.pb.gz http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile
aws s3 cp /tmp/pprof-2765437890.pb.gz s3://redwood-nightly/2765437890/pprof-ken.pb.gz
```

ken: run reproduced. attaching short log lines: `p95: 342ms -> 438ms`, and I've uploaded artifacts to s3 path above. starting pprof now.

opsbot: note: alert annotated on incident tracker (INC-2026) and linked to channel.

marta: nice. devon — once your revert branch is up can you run the harness with the same commit range? if revert brings p95 back, we can fast-track a rollback to the patch.

devon: revert run finished: p95 back within 3% of baseline. no other changes. pushing revert as temp mitigation.

bri: confirmed on my end too. LGTM for revert as an emergency hotfix. we should add an integration test for eviction-frequency under small-batch load.

marta: agreed. next actions: (a) open PR to revert w/ rollback tag and postmortem notes, (b) add regression test in nightly-harness, (c) follow-up for a cleaner fix on eviction heuristics. I'll file the follow-ups and add owners.

ken: I'll draft the rollback PR and notify infra to schedule a canary deploy to Dedicated tomorrow morning.

marta: thanks all. marking this triaged — will update INC-2026 and archive artifacts. :white_check_mark:
